The current integrated control is `8d08ba48b554a84b9920e349e6d4c69dccd6c0dd`, v4 main after #457. A detached control checkout is retained at `../wvm-v4-issue358-control`; the candidate is `issue-358-compact-constant-schedule`. The older `da764d0` audit and benchmark WVM fixtures retain historical provenance. The benchmark implementation publication is `6f2e4cd9e2f092433a584645e573d818ecaca42b`; its sibling working-tree edits are not used as authoritative source or modified.

The user authorized completion of #358, with agents at appropriate model levels. The provider and constant-kernel numerical work use the existing higher-capability agents; a smaller-model agent inventories fixtures and build dependencies. No #454 sampling capability is inferred from this optimization.

## Prospective adoption protocol

This protocol precedes candidate timing. Artifact paths, source and executable hashes, effective worker settings and exact invocations will be frozen in a machine-readable execution manifest before each campaign. Functional tests and exploratory correctness runs are not adoption measurements.

- Native standalone complete flux uses four calibration profiles: hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic constant stratification at 256×256×129 and 512×512×257, antialiasing on, domains 15 km × 15 km × 1300 m, N0=0.0052 s^-1, latitude 45 degrees, nonzero reference-time offset 123.5 s. MATLAB authors deterministic input and independent expected flux. Exact coefficient generation and file hashes are frozen before runs.
- Additional functional cases cover small odd/even/nonsquare grids, unequal domains, antialiasing off, explicit vertical truncation, zero/Nyquist/inertial/geostrophic/mean-density modes, F/G endpoints, direct and derivative fields, ordinary/velocity-producing/velocity-consuming/spatial-tendency-only/scalar paths, aliases, invalid inputs, failure cleanup and repeated ownership release.
- The complete-model timing profiles are two constant-stratification configurations at 32×24×33 with coefficient-only output and with particles/tracers/dense output. Fixed RK4 work is matched exactly. Adaptive restart/output scientific controls are separate from fixed-work timing attribution.
- Worker screening is bounded: horizontal outer workers start at the host performance-core count (12), FFTW horizontal internal workers 1, Type-I internal workers at physical-core count (16), coefficient workers 2. Pointwise candidates are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12. One policy must apply across both sizes and hydrostatic choices. Small-work serial dispatch may use a predeclared work-size threshold, not profile-specific tuning. Only if topology implementation requires another candidate will its reason and bounded set be recorded before timing it.
- Screen candidates with two excluded warmups and three uninstrumented complete-flux samples per profile. Select by geometric mean; within 1% choose fewer workers, then less owned memory, then candidate order. Retain every failed/negative screen. Screens do not establish adoption.
- The worker-selection geometric mean weights the four native and four MATLAB-loaded calibration profiles equally. Both boundaries use the same pointwise candidates and one selected policy. The frozen native control uses its ordinary Release CMake build with 16 FFTW workers; the MEX control and candidates use the production O3/native flags and pinned macOS 13.3 target. Each comparison is within a boundary with matched build flags. This clarification was recorded before the first worker screen.
- Final standalone evidence uses eight alternating fresh-process control/candidate pairs for each declared timing profile, two excluded warmups and seven uninstrumented samples per flux process. Use each process's median. The primary point estimate is the geometric mean of paired candidate/control ratios. A deterministic 10,000-resample paired bootstrap, seed 358, supplies a two-sided 95% interval by resampling complete pair indices within each profile. No optional reruns triggered solely by an unfavorable decision; invalid interrupted runs retain their logs and are replaced only with a documented environmental cause.
- Default adoption requires a geometric complete-flux ratio at most 0.90, no declared timing profile ratio above 1.03, and the overall complete-flux interval's upper endpoint below 1.00. Complete-model outputs and step/RHS work must match their scientific controls. Setup and stage-instrumented calls are measured separately from the authoritative uninstrumented calls.
- Owned persistent and scratch capacities, including descriptors, phase, plans/provider lower bounds, executor management, optional velocity buffers and configured scalar storage, must not exceed matched control. No hidden retained full-spectrum arena may be excluded from this ledger. Report unobservable provider allocations separately. Fresh-process lifetime peak RSS comes from child-exit resource usage, after output close and destruction; paired geometric median RSS ratio must be at most 1.00 with a 95% paired upper bound at most 1.03 to accommodate measurement uncertainty. This is the predeclared interpretation of no measured process-memory regression, not a license to add owned storage.
- Large schedule/control flux agreement retains maximum scale-normalized error ≤2e-12 and relative L2 ≤1e-12; independent MATLAB cross-implementation comparison retains both bounds ≤1e-10. Existing small-fixture thresholds remain unchanged. These are distinct comparisons, not interchangeable tolerances.
- MATLAB-loaded execution is qualified separately with the same candidate policy and a matched control MEX. No process-wide BLAS environment mutation from MEX; no overlapping executing worker teams. If the standalone policy cannot pass MATLAB-loaded timing/memory/scientific controls, retain the existing preview default and state that scoped result explicitly.
- Performance campaigns run without competing MATLAB/build workloads after coordination. Setup, flux/RHS, integration, output, adapters/data movement, retained capacities and complete-lifetime RSS are reported separately. Current Linux/reference/sanitizer/source-consumer checks qualify source compatibility; they do not establish a native speedup on unmeasured platforms.

If any adoption gate fails, preserve the current production default. Retain the candidate evidence and issue a precise rejected/deferred outcome with focused follow-up rather than describing functionality or a 3% non-regression pass as benchmark adoption.

Integration/control profile ratios are 1.185672, 1.196659, 1.206686 and 1.193681, exceeding the 1.03 gate. Overall integration ratio is 1.195651, paired 95% interval [1.180051,1.209747]. - **Decision: retain the frozen default.** The completed failing mandatory gate makes further expensive adoption measurements unnecessary. The remaining native campaign was intentionally stopped after three complete pairs for one profile; its fourth control process was terminated and all logs retained. Final MATLAB-loaded timing was not started. Neither partial campaign nor screening is described as final large-flux adoption evidence. Follow-up #460 owns small-work policy qualification. The frozen prospective protocol, exact measurements and early-rejection explanation are retained in `.github/ci-evidence/issue-358-adoption`.
